differences.what: massing from the plate's own camera: the front between the south gable at the left and the north corner block at the right, the round tower right of the gable under a slated cone with a finial, the very steep slated roof with iron cresting, and the north flank receding to the right; the front's two corners, the flank's rear corner, the tower's axis and the door land within 8.5 px of the plate (4.0 px RMS)
the tall stack rising off the north flank behind the corner block, standing where the plate draws it and to about its height

the storeys: with the cornice placed, the plate draws the chamber belt about 58 px (some 3 m) higher on the north corner than the record's 6.15 m and the walls' foot well above the record's grade, so it makes the walls about 0.8 of the record's height for their width; the row elevations (elevations_c1914_front) agree in direction, a principal storey near 4.8 m and a chamber storey near 3.6 m against the record's 4.3 and 4.35 m; two drawings against a photograph: the photograph (chicagology_photo) reads the principal and chamber storeys up the north corner block's front corner, one vertical at one distance and so at one scale, as 4.3 and 4.35 m (395 and 400 px), and the record builds the photograph's reading; a gap the pictures disagree about is within tolerance (T-3153, T-3290)

the south gable: drawn as a tall stone wall gable rising through the roof over a chamber pair and the arched pair of the principal floor, two round heads with colonnettes under one arch; built a low coped gable at the eave, its copings now carrying three crockets a rake between the kneelers' pinnacles and the apex finial (T-3293) and its principal pair round-headed (T-3292); the gable's height through the roof and the enclosing arch over the pair are not built (T-3294)

the tower's top: the plate carries the tower a full stage over the main cornice, with its own lights and pinnacles, under a tall slated spire; the build springs a broader cone about 1 m over the cornice (the photograph's chicagology_photo record reads the cone lower still, so the two pictures, thirty years apart, are to be weighed against each other)

the dormers' ornament: the plate's are stone wall dormers with crocketed gables and pinnacles rising off the cornice; now built faced in the front's stone, a stone coping up each rake with crockets on its back (two a rake on the north dormer, three on the south), a square pinnacle engaged at each edge of the face from the cornice past the gable's foot under a cap and a pyramid, and a turned finial at the apex (T-3293)

the dormers' places: the plate draws the second dormer on the north flank and both faces rising in the wall's plane; the build stands both on the street face, as the photograph (chicagology_photo) shows them, each face on the cornice 0.2 m in front of the wall's plane

the entrance: the door now stands in a deep round-arched recess under a moulded voussoir ring and keystone (T-3292), as the plate draws it; the plate's carved capitals either side are not built (T-3294, on the photograph's record)

the corbelled corner turret at the north flank's front end (x 350-372, y 150-310 px of the cut): built (T-3290) from the photograph, a round of one storey over the attic belt under a slated cone, which the plate's camera puts behind the north stack; the plate draws it taller, two stages corbelled out from the chamber floor with a pendant under the corbel, where the photograph (chicagology_photo), thirty years later and from the same place, shows one stage rising off the attic belt: the pictures disagree, so within tolerance (T-3153), and the photograph's turret is built
the low iron railing along the walk before the house
colour and the stone's tone: the plate is a monochrome engraving, so the brownstone's colour is not compared
the south flank, the rear and the roof's rear faces
the walk, the trees, the carriage and the figures, and the brick neighbour at the left

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
